LESSON: READING 12.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.2: Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading, part of Strand 12 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why are songs and poems more enjoyable than reading a book? 2. How can we make a poem or song more interesting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. participate in a reader’s theatre and read solo or choral poems, using correct stress,

2. sing along as a video of poetry recitation or song plays with the lyrics provided, using the correct rhythm,

3. identify words, phrases, and proverbs used in the song or poem,

4. make predictions about events in a poem on environmental conservation by observing the picture or title,

5. answer direct and inferential questions from a comprehension passage,

6. create mental images by viewing pictures or events in a poem or 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. participate in a reader’s theatre and read solo or choral poems, using correct stress,
2. sing along as a video of poetry recitation or song plays with the lyrics provided, using the correct rhythm,
3. identify words, phrases, and proverbs used in the song or poem,
4. make predictions about events in a poem on environmental conservation by observing the picture or title,
5. answer direct and inferential questions from a comprehension passage,
6. create mental images by viewing pictures or events in a poem or 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: The learner’s ability to confidently plan and carry out tasks independently is enhanced as they

engage in the readers theatre activity with peers.

• Learning to Learn: The learner’s ability to grasp concepts on their own is developed as they share what they have

learnt by participating in a reader’s theatre.

Values:
Patriotism: is fostered as the learner acquires knowledge about his or her county’s environment and how to conserve

it for future generations as they interact with texts on environmental conservation.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Environmental Conservation: The learner’s knowledge on preservation of the environment is enhanced as they

make predictions about events in a poem on environmental conservation.

• Life Skills (Creative Thinking): The learner is able to think creatively as they engage in the task of giving the

meaning of new words in the poem from the way they have been used in the text.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the skill of intensive reading to their learning in Kiswahili.
